amendments.side_finding: an encoder that can only ever emit ONE of a field's two legal values does not make that field emittable; recorded as a db/tool defect (DEF-0170-1 class).
amendments.stage: before any build, census or device run
amendments.what: H1 for falu2i.imm_flag rewritten from a mantissa-LSB model to an operand-SIZE-bit model
amendments.why: tools/agx-isa/isadb.py::imm_decode uses a 3-BIT mantissa (m=(b1>>1)&0x7) and never reads b1 bit 0, while imm_encode hard-sets it -- so the drafted oracle was unsatisfiable by construction. Recorded in PRE_REGISTRATION.md sec.9 rather than silently corrected.

cfdiv.why: n4_cf_word.b3 -- the 04 01 00 <b3> control word was located before pop_reconverge / threadgroup_barrier in divergent-CF kernels; this is nested data-dependent divergence with reconvergence points.

deadsrc.why: irotate.b2 + simd_ballot.cache + simd_shuffle.cache -- all three are the same 0x54 operand byte at byte+2, and db.json's vocabulary for a byte in that role (falu_acc, RT-1a-FIX) is 'a source cache / LAST-USE hint'. Every carrier ever swept for these reuses its sources, so they are ONE carrier in that dimension. Here every operand is loaded, used once, and dead immediately after.

deriv.why: tex_deriv.dstsrc -- the ONLY field left blocking tex_deriv, and the ISA database has never had a carrier authored for it: every previous 0x37 in the corpus was incidental to implicit-LOD sampling. Eight independent derivatives of three varyings with different gradients, each in its own output channel, across BOTH axis values (0x92 dfdx / 0x90 dfdy) and the fwidth abs+add form -- so the arm list spans the axis dimension inside one program and a dst- or src-register redirect is an exact numeric change, not noise.

fimm.why: falu2i.imm_flag -- bit8 sits INSIDE db.json's own imm_decode(). The dimension it controls is the decoded immediate, so this carrier spans the minifloat domain (1/32 .. 30) under fadd and fmul rather than using one constant as EXP-0138's single carrier did.

fimm2.why: falu2i.imm_flag -- structurally different arm: negative immediates (imm_sign=1), fma-shaped uses, and immediates applied to a freshly LOADED operand (the mods==0xC0 form of EXP-0101).

ibhalf.why: [from EXP-0163] imageblock_store.src with a HALF attachment format.

ibmrt.why: [from EXP-0163] imageblock_store.src with THREE render targets.

ibsamp.why: [from EXP-0163] imageblock_store.src baseline shape (single RGBA32Float attachment, texture-sampling fragment program).

rot.why: irotate.b2 -- EXP-0166 recommendation 4. EXP-0146's arm reached 32 of 256 encodings through assemble()'s OR defect; this sweep patches bytes directly and the raw is checked for 256 DISTINCT byte strings. Sources are reused after the rotate (live-source side of the last-use dimension).

rot2.why: irotate.b2 -- second structurally different rotate carrier: results feed the SIMD network and a threadgroup round-trip, sources are 16-bit and lane-derived.

sball.why: [from EXP-0163] simd_ballot.cache / simd_shuffle.cache live-source reference arm; every ballot form the language offers, each result consumed several times.

sdiv.why: [from EXP-0163] SIMD ops under a partially active mask.

srnarrow.why: get_sr.form -- the SCALAR-SR control for srwide. Same kernel shape, same output surface, only the SR WIDTH differs, which is the dimension db.json says form controls.

srwide.why: get_sr.form -- db.json calls form a datapath/WIDTH modifier 'set for the position-in-grid SR family'. This carrier reads ONLY the multi-component (uint3) SR family, so form is natively 1 on its occurrences. Its controlled sibling srnarrow reads only scalar SRs. EXP-0140 swept form on one carrier; EXP-0164 withheld it as never-moved-on-one-carrier.

stype.why: [from EXP-0163] the mode==0x06 rotate / shuffle-and-fill form and the 16/64-bit operand widths; the only carrier on which simd_shuffle.rsv9 ever moved.

texmix.why: tex_sample.coord -- the same descriptor reached through three operation kinds (explicit-LOD sample, gather, integer read) in one program, so a coord verdict is not a property of one kind. Every operation is derivative-free.

texread.why: tex_sample.coord -- EXP-0155's movement did not reproduce (73-93% cross-run agreement). coord is a REGISTER INDEX, so a swept value points the coordinate operand at an arbitrary register; on a filtered sample that feeds garbage derivatives, an arbitrary LOD and an arbitrary wrap. read(uint2) has no sampler, derivative, LOD or filter, so the per-value outcome should be run-invariant.

tgat.why: frame_marker_compact.b1 -- the 2-byte 60 <b1> word was length-anchored in a threadgroup-atomics kernel and has never been swept on hardware.

vmany.why: vary_slot.slot -- 16 scalar varyings force slots past 7, where the slot descriptor has something to say. EXP-0155 saw slot move 3 of 256 in one run and 0 in the other (noise) on a 4-varying carrier.

vsrc.why: vary_slot.slot -- varyings sourced from memory / immediates / computed values rather than one class.

clean_room.inputs: kernels/*.metal (ours) + the machine code the public Metal API produced from them

co_variance_check_rule3: run.py splices ONLY the instruction under test at a frozen absolute offset and observes fixed surfaces at probe points chosen before the run. No read-back register, probe pixel, output index or surface is a function of the swept value. The EXP-0140 failure mode (uniform_mov.dst read back through device_store(data_reg=D) where D WAS the swept dst) cannot occur.

declined_with_reason.cubearray_coord_const.b3: UNSWEEPABLE, not merely untested. EXP-0148 found the descriptor fires 0 times in 1080 corpus files under both the strict and the resync walk: its `f0 c0 04` signature in k_tex_array_cube sits at offset 48, INTERIOR to the 12-byte tex_addr_setup token spanning 40..52, so it can never be reached. Its only exercise is the literal 4-byte string in roundtrip_test.py -- and a round trip is not an emitter gate (FIELD-SWEEP-PROTOCOL sec.3b). There is no program in which to splice b3. RECOMMENDATION: this is a descriptor-existence question for the orchestrator (delete or re-anchor), not a sweep.
declined_with_reason.half_alu_fma12.ext: BLOCKED BY A DESCRIPTOR DEFECT. half_alu_fma12 is flagged `emit_unsafe` in db.json because its modelled length OVER-CONSUMES the following instruction's leader (FIELD-SWEEP-PROTOCOL sec.6 known list), and `ext` is the 64-bit unmodelled remainder -- i.e. exactly the bytes the length defect puts in doubt. Sweeping it would sweep the NEXT instruction. The length must be fixed before the field means anything.
declined_with_reason.imageblock_store.src (as an INSTRUCTION: SWEPT (tier 2) but it does NOT close the instruction: the live worklist now shows imageblock_store TWO fields away (`src` + `b4`), and `b4` is EXP-0163's INERT-ROBUST result, which rule 8 caps at single-template-inference. Promoting `src` is a field win only.
declined_with_reason.mesh_out_src.sel: NO CARRIER. mesh_out_src is MESH-stage-only and harness/gfrun2.m has no mesh pipeline (MTLMeshRenderPipelineDescriptor) at all. Authoring one is a harness project with its own pre-registration, not a field sweep; attempting it inside this experiment would mean building an unvalidated render path and a frozen contract at the same time.
declined_with_reason.ret.scoreboard / dev_scoreboard_fence.sc: PROMOTION DECLINED IN ADVANCE (they are still swept, for the record). Both are ORDERING controls -- an execution/scoreboard-wait mask and a memory-fence scope. This harness has no ordering observable: it reads back after command-buffer completion, which flushes. A carrier that moves therefore proves GENERAL sensitivity to the byte, not ordering-specific power, which is why three prior experiments declined to promote this family. We decline for the same reason and say so, rather than promoting on a general-sensitivity result.

device_load_hazard_EXP0169.detection: the >=99% per-value cross-run gate is a nondeterminism detector: an intermittently landing load cannot reproduce the same per-value partition twice.
device_load_hazard_EXP0169.knowing_exception: fimm2 keeps the load-sourced mods==0xC0 form deliberately (EXP-0101) and is flagged as carrying the hazard.
device_load_hazard_EXP0169.prevention: k_fimm, k_srwide, k_srnarrow seed operands from special registers through ALU only; k_texread, k_texmix, k_deriv declare NO buffer and derive everything from the interpolated [[position]]. These carriers contain no device_load at all.

match_overlap_check.handling: the harness patches via its own clear-then-set mask, not assemble(), then re-decodes every patched instruction; a value that no longer decodes as the same mnemonic is recorded `undecodable` and excluded from encodable_range.
match_overlap_check.result: of this experiment's fields exactly ONE overlaps its own descriptor match: irotate.b2 (width 8, bits 16 and 18..23 pinned by match -> 1 free bit -> 2 LEGAL VALUES of 256 dispatched). All others are match-disjoint.

note_on_revision: CODEX/SUBAGENT_BRIEF: captures are validated against these AUTHORED BLOB HASHES, not against live HEAD. Sibling experiments landing commits is not contamination (EXP-0082).

pinned_isa_db.resolution: AGXRE_REPO=$HOME/agxre/EXP-0172 -> tools/agx-isa/{db.json,isadb.py} are copies of work/frozen/*
pinned_isa_db.why: EXP-0169 found the neo's SHARED tools/agx-isa/db.json stale: 1036 fields vs the repo's 1060, with falu2.srcA_class/srcB_class replaced by mod_lo, reached by a _find_isadb() fall-through. This experiment pins its own snapshot and resolves it EXPLICITLY via AGXRE_REPO=$HOME/agxre/EXP-0172; the neo's shared tools/ is not touched.

promotion_gate.detection_power: arm must show a status-OK, SAME-MNEMONIC control that moved the observation
promotion_gate.distinct_bytes_definition: count of DISTINCT `bytes` strings observed in raw/, never the dispatched-value count
promotion_gate.encodable_range_definition: the swept values whose patched bytes RE-DECODE as the same mnemonic (DEF-0170-1)
forbidden_evidence: roundtrip_test.py / rt_ok (a round trip is not an emitter gate)
promotion_gate.never_moving_field: promotable only if carriers differ in the dimension the field controls (rule 2)
